The system shall prioritize incident response work after life safety work.
The system shall prioritize work tied to statutory deadlines or continuity of operations after life safety work and incident response.
The system shall allow lower-priority collaboration work to be deferred or rerouted to protect the shared service.
The system shall allow bulk processing work to be deferred or rerouted to protect the shared service.
The system shall permit exceptions for agency-specific mission work or workload types that have a formal critical designation.
A capacity exception during congestion shall be controlled by an incident or capacity management process with a named decision-maker.
Approval of a capacity exception shall be based on current demand.
After the event has started, approval may still be granted if the situation is actively unfolding and delay would cause real operational harm.
A post-event approval for a capacity exception shall be used only when the exception was necessary to keep the service functioning during an urgent situation.
Once a post-event approval for a capacity exception is granted, it shall be logged right away with the approver, the affected workload, the reason it was necessary, and its duration.
A capacity exception shall have a short time limit.
A capacity exception shall undergo a follow-up review to decide whether it should be extended, converted to a standing exception, or ended.
The default exception duration shall be very short.
The exception may become a standing exception only if the need is recurring, well-documented, and accepted as part of the agency’s normal operating profile with the right approvals.
The trigger for post-event approval shall be a documented operational impact that is already happening.
